meta.title: Augustine on the restlessness you can never quite shake
meta.search_phrase: our hearts are restless augustine meaning

beats.text: Before he was a saint, Augustine chased everything: status, pleasure, clever arguments, love.
Each goal, once reached, left the same strange hollow. The hunger simply moved on to the next thing.
He began to suspect the restlessness itself was the clue — that it was pointing somewhere.
Maybe no finite thing could fill it, because it was shaped for something infinite.
"You have made us for Yourself," he wrote, "and our heart is restless until it rests in You."
You don't have to share his faith to feel the ache he named — that nothing you get is ever quite enough.
The restlessness isn't a flaw to fix. It's a question asking what you're really made for.

source_note: Quote: Confessions, trans. E. B. Pusey (public domain).
